metadata.title: What Would Have to Be True
metadata.audience: Anyone who has ever trusted a status message — students, engineers, and laypeople alike
metadata.greeting_note: Chosen by synthesis test, not taste — am_onyx renders Annyeong as "Annual" and Konnichiwa as "Konnashiwo"; Shalom survives intact and is the only candidate that also left "Liam" correctly pronounced beside it. Wagwan stays Bear's under IN-FOR-BEAR LAW.
metadata.source: Nik Bear Brown, INFO 7375 — Computational Skepticism for AI, Chapter 1: The Skeptic's Toolkit. Scope: the Descartes move only.
metadata.one_idea: Radical doubt is not a mood about a claim. It is a question that converts a claim into a list of conditions somebody can check — and it matters most when the output looks right.
metadata.tts_note: Every figure is written as words; no letter-by-letter sequences. "Day-cart" is a phonetic respelling used in narration_text ONLY (am_onyx says "Discard's" for the correct spelling). Never on screen. See VOICE-QA.md.
metadata.voice_note: am_onyx measured as the darkest English voice available (spectral centroid 1748 Hz). am_puck is 2883 Hz — 65% brighter — at the same top ASR tier, and is already a sanctioned voice in the channels table. NOTE: the ai-explainer channels table pairs claude-liam with am_onyx, so this is a deliberate deviation from the channel default, made on explicit request.
